Article 3
Paragraph (1) Sufficiently clear.
Paragraph (2) Sufficiently clear.
Paragraph (3) Letter a What is meant by the "prevention" aspect is a protection strategy effort through:
a. Primary prevention, all people, families, communities and the state in efforts to increase the ability of knowledge, understanding and ensure that violence against women and children does not occur, including policy socialization, adequate services, supportive workplace policies, and life skills training for women and children. What is meant by life skills training includes conflict resolution without violence, stress management skills, resource management, effective decision making, effective interpersonal communication, guidance on psychosocial development of women and children.
4 2015
b. Secondary prevention, aimed at community groups with high risk in efforts to increase skills, including training and victim services to ensure that violence against women and children does not occur in the next generation.
Activities carried out here include conducting home visits for parents who have just had children to conduct self assessment whether they are at risk of committing violence against children in the future.
c. Tertiary prevention, intended to increase parenting abilities that ensure that violence against women and children does not recur, what is done here is integrated services for women and children who are victims of violence, through counseling, stress management training.
Letter b What is meant by the "service and assistance" aspect is immediate activities and actions carried out by professionals and assistants in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
Letter c Sufficiently clear.
Letter d What is meant by the "empowerment" aspect is the process of increasing the role of the community to participate in the implementation of protection for women and children victims of acts of violence which aims to obtain access and participation in the process of protection of women and children broadly.
5 2015 Number 4

Article I
Several provisions in Regional Regulation of Bantul Regency Number 15 of 2013 concerning Protection of Children and Women Victims of Violence (Regional Gazette of Bantul Regency Year 2013 Number 15, Supplement to Regional Gazette of Bantul Regency Number 28), are amended as follows:
1. The provisions of Article 1 are amended, to read as follows: Article 1
1. Government is the Central Government.
2. Region is Bantul Regency.
3. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of regional government administration.
5 2015
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Bantul Regency as an element of Regional Government administration.
5. Regent is the Regent of Bantul.
6. Regional Apparatus Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is the regional apparatus work unit of Bantul Regency.
7. Woman is a person who is female by sex and a person who is recognized by law as a woman.
8. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 years of age, including a child still in the womb.
9. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, and psychological, threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life against the victim.
10. Violence against women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
11. Violence against children is any action that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, psychologically, sexually, neglect, exploitation, economically, and other violence.
12. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death.
13. Psychological Violence is any act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person.
14. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
15. Economic Violence is any act that neglects family members in the form of not providing proper living care or maintenance.
16. Exploitation of Children is any act involving children in activities that may harm their welfare and development or endanger the safety of children with the aim of enabling others to obtain economic, sexual, social, or political benefits, including if it contains restrictions or elimination of opportunities for children to obtain their rights.
6 2015
17. Sexual harassment is any action with sexual nuances conveyed through physical or non-physical contact that targets sexual body parts or a person's sexuality, including by using whistles, winking, comments or sexually nuanced speech, displaying pornographic materials and sexual desires, pinching or touching body parts, movements or gestures that are sexual in nature resulting in feelings of discomfort, offense, feeling degraded in dignity, and possibly causing health and safety problems.
18. Victim is a Child and Woman who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence occurring in the area of Bantul Regency.
19. Prevention is direct efforts made by the Regional Government to prevent acts of violence against women and children.
20. Protection is all service actions to guarantee and protect the rights of victims of violence organized by the Integrated Service Center.
21. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security for women carried out by family members, police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
22. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
23. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
24. Women's Empowerment is any effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social capacity, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities.
25. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has expertise in accompanying victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of violence victims.
26. Spiritual guidance is accompaniment in the form of services for spiritual strengthening so that sick people can rise to be closer to God so that feelings of calm, security arise, and mental health is achieved.
27. Judicial body is the general judiciary that has the authority to receive, examine, and adjudicate, as well as resolve every case submitted to it, to realize law enforcement and justice.
7 2015
28. Prosecution is the action of the public prosecutor to transfer a case to the competent district court in the manner and according to the procedure regulated by law with a request to be examined and decided by a judge in a court session.
29. Lawsuit is notification accompanied by a request by an interested party to a judge to take action according to law against someone who has harmed them in a civil manner.
30. Institution is an agency/office/body/office within the scope of regional government and/or non-governmental organization (NGO) that provides assistance to victims of violence.
31. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence.
32. Regional Action Plan is the foundation and guideline for related agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in order to carry out activities for the prevention and protection of children and women victims of violence.
33. Safe House is a shelter for victims, during the assistance process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers of perpetrators in accordance with predetermined standards.
34. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitutes who can provide protection and fulfillment of victims' needs.
35. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter abbreviated as SOP is standard steps that must be taken in protecting victims starting from complaints/identification, rehabilitation, health, social rehabilitation, legal services up to repatriation and social reintegration of witnesses and/or victims.
36. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
37. Household is husband, wife, and children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, foster care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household.
38. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
39. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD is the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of Bantul Regency
40. Gender responsive budget is a budget that provides and accommodates justice and equality for women and men to access and obtain access, as well as benefits from development programs and participate in decision-making processes and have control over resources.
8 2015
41. Forum for Protection of Violence Victims hereinafter abbreviated as FPKK is a coordination forum for handling Child and Women victims of violence whose implementation is carried out in a networked manner.
2. The provisions of Article 2 are amended, to read as follows: Article 2 The principles of organizing protection of children and women from acts of violence are:
a. respect and fulfillment of victims' rights; b. justice and gender equality;
c. non-discrimination;
d. the best interests of victims; and
e. empowerment.
3. The provisions of Article 3 are amended, to read as follows: Article 3 (1) Forms of violence, among others:
a. physical;
b. psychological;
c. sexual;
d. neglect;
e. exploitation; and/or
f. other violence.
(2) The objectives of protection of Children and Women from acts of violence are:
a. to prevent and eliminate all forms of violence and exploitation against children and women occurring in the family and community environment;
b. to seek recovery and social reintegration of children and women victims of violence;
c. to provide services to children and women victims of violence, reporters, and witnesses;
d. to empower women victims of violence; and
e. to increase community participation.
(3) The organization of protection of children and women from acts of violence as referred to in paragraph (1), includes aspects of: a. prevention;
b. service and assistance;
c. social reintegration; and
d. empowerment.
9 2015
4. The provisions of Article 6 are amended, to read as follows: Article 6 The organization of protection of children and women victims of violence is the obligation of:
a. Regional Government;
b. Village Government;
c. community;
d. family; and
e. parents.
5. The provisions of letter d and letter e paragraph (1) of Article 7 are amended, to read as follows:

Article 7
(1) To implement the provisions as referred to in Article 6 letter a, the Regional Government implements victim protection efforts, in the form of:
a. formulating policies regarding the protection of Children and Women from all forms of violence and discrimination;
b. preparing program and activity planning;
c. providing support for facilities and infrastructure;
d. allocating special gender-responsive budgets that support the protection of children and women victims of violence;
e. establishing and facilitating PPT;
f. establishing and facilitating FPKK; and
g. conducting monitoring and evaluation.
(2) In the implementation of the Regional Government's obligations as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regional Government prepares a Regional Action Plan as a basis for SKPD in implementing protection for victims.
(3) The Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (2), constitutes part of the Regional Medium-Term Development Plan (RPJMD).
(4) Further provisions regarding the Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be further regulated by Regent Regulation.
6. The title of Part One CHAPTER IV is deleted.
10 2015
7. The provisions of Article 13 are amended, to read as follows: Article 13 (1) In order to provide services and protection to victims of violence, the Regional Government establishes PPT.
(2) PPT as referred to in paragraph (1) has the duties, principal tasks, and functions of providing protection to Children and Women from violence, which consists of fields.
(3) PPT as referred to in paragraph (1) is tasked with providing services and protection to children and women victims of violence.
(4) In the event that PPT does not have facilities to provide services and protection as referred to in paragraph (3), then children and women victims of violence are referred through a network system within the FPKK forum.
(5) PPT as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be stipulated by Regent Regulation.
8. The provisions of Article 24 are amended, to read as follows: Article 24 Further provisions regarding the development, mechanism and networked working relationships of PPT as referred to in Article 13 shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.
9. The provisions of Article 26 are amended, to read as follows: Article 26 Prevention efforts are also carried out by:
a. the community;
b. the family; and
c. educational institutions.
11 2015
10. The provisions of paragraph (1), paragraph (2), paragraph (3) and paragraph (5) of Article 40 are amended, to read as follows:

Article 25
Paragraph (1) Sufficiently clear Paragraph (2) Point a What is meant by "network" includes family partners, dasawisma, family groups that exist in the community.
What is meant by "coordination" includes planning, implementation and monitoring of violence prevention programs.
Point b What is meant by "violence prevention system" includes mapping of locations or areas prone to violence and conducting promotive and preventive efforts to the community.
7 2015 Point c What is meant by "Critical education about the rights of children and women" is an effort to build awareness of children and women about their rights.
The purpose of implementing critical education is to be able to help decision-making and not become victims of repeated violence.
Forms of critical education for the community consist of: trainings on gender equality and justice, education on reproductive health for women, and providing understanding of laws and regulations on the Elimination of Domestic Violence and Child Protection.
Point d Socialization can be conducted through mass media, electronic media, and direct counseling to the community.
Number 15

I. GENERAL
As a manifestation of the Regional Government's responsibility in taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce, and eliminate all forms of violence against children and women, Regional Regulation of Bantul Regency Number 15 of 2013 concerning Protection of Children and Women Victims of Violence has been established.
Up to the present time, the aforementioned Regional Regulation has been implemented in the administration of government in the Region. However, in accordance with the supervision mechanism for regional legal products, the Regional Government of the Special Region of Yogyakarta has provided clarification on Regional Regulation of Bantul Regency Number 15 of 2013 concerning Protection of Children and Women Victims of Violence. From the results of the aforementioned clarification, there are several substantive changes that must be followed up with an Amendment to the Regional Regulation.
2 2015 Based on the aforementioned considerations, Regional Regulation of Bantul Regency Number 15 of 2013 concerning Protection of Children and Women Victims of Violence needs to be amended in its Articles and explanations.

Article 2
Letter a What is meant by "respect and fulfillment of victims' rights" is a series of actions to respect, appreciate and ensure the fulfillment of victims' rights.
Letter b What is meant by "gender justice and equality" is a process to be fair to men and women and equal conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so as to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, social and cultural activities, National defense and security and equality in enjoying the results of such development.
Letter c What is meant by "non-discrimination" is an attitude and treatment toward victims by not making distinctions based on age, gender, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups.
Letter d What is meant by "the best interests of victims" is that all actions of recovery, rehabilitation, reunification concerning victims carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, must be the primary consideration.
3 2015 Letter e What is meant by "empowerment" is the strengthening of victims of violence to be able to work and do business independently after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
Number 3

Article 26
Letter a Prevention efforts in the community include: fostering environmental awareness of acts of violence occurring in their environment.
Letter b Prevention efforts in the family and/or closest relatives can be carried out by strengthening resilience within the household such as: practicing religious values, managing household time, and communication among family members Letter c Educational institutions can participate in efforts to provide punishments that are educational in nature, endeavoring to eliminate provisions that do not side with victims of violence.
Number 10

Article II
This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of promulgation.
In order that every person shall know of it, the promulgation of this Regional Regulation is ordered by placement in the Regional Gazette of Bantul Regency.
Enacted in Bantul on the date of 30 December 2015

I. GENERAL
As a manifestation of the Regional Government's responsibility in taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce, and eliminate all forms of violence against children and women, Regional Regulation of Bantul Regency Number 15 of 2013 concerning Protection of Children and Women Victims of Violence has been established.
Up to the present time, the aforementioned Regional Regulation has been implemented in the administration of government in the Region. However, in accordance with the supervision mechanism for regional legal products, the Regional Government of the Special Region of Yogyakarta has provided clarification on Regional Regulation of Bantul Regency Number 15 of 2013 concerning Protection of Children and Women Victims of Violence. From the results of the aforementioned clarification, there are several substantive changes that must be followed up with an Amendment to the Regional Regulation.
2 2015 Based on the aforementioned considerations, Regional Regulation of Bantul Regency Number 15 of 2013 concerning Protection of Children and Women Victims of Violence needs to be amended in its Articles and explanations.

I. GENERAL
As a manifestation of the Regional Government's responsibility in taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce, and eliminate all forms of violence against children and women, Regional Regulation of Bantul Regency Number 15 of 2013 concerning Protection of Children and Women Victims of Violence has been established.
Up to the present time, the aforementioned Regional Regulation has been implemented in the administration of government in the Region. However, in accordance with the supervision mechanism for regional legal products, the Regional Government of the Special Region of Yogyakarta has provided clarification on Regional Regulation of Bantul Regency Number 15 of 2013 concerning Protection of Children and Women Victims of Violence. From the results of the aforementioned clarification, there are several substantive changes that must be followed up with an Amendment to the Regional Regulation.
2 2015 Based on the aforementioned considerations, Regional Regulation of Bantul Regency Number 15 of 2013 concerning Protection of Children and Women Victims of Violence needs to be amended in its Articles and explanations.

Article I

1. The provisions of Article 1 are amended, to read as follows: Article 1
1. Government is the Central Government.
2. Region is Bantul Regency.
3. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of regional government administration.
5 2015
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Bantul Regency as an element of Regional Government administration.
5. Regent is the Regent of Bantul.
6. Regional Apparatus Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is the regional apparatus work unit of Bantul Regency.
7. Woman is a person who is female by sex and a person who is recognized by law as a woman.
8. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 years of age, including a child still in the womb.
9. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, and psychological, threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life against the victim.
10. Violence against women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
11. Violence against children is any action that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, psychologically, sexually, neglect, exploitation, economically, and other violence.
12. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death.
13. Psychological Violence is any act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person.
14. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
15. Economic Violence is any act that neglects family members in the form of not providing proper living care or maintenance.
16. Exploitation of Children is any act involving children in activities that may harm their welfare and development or endanger the safety of children with the aim of enabling others to obtain economic, sexual, social, or political benefits, including if it contains restrictions or elimination of opportunities for children to obtain their rights.
6 2015
17. Sexual harassment is any action with sexual nuances conveyed through physical or non-physical contact that targets sexual body parts or a person's sexuality, including by using whistles, winking, comments or sexually nuanced speech, displaying pornographic materials and sexual desires, pinching or touching body parts, movements or gestures that are sexual in nature resulting in feelings of discomfort, offense, feeling degraded in dignity, and possibly causing health and safety problems.
18. Victim is a Child and Woman who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence occurring in the area of Bantul Regency.
19. Prevention is direct efforts made by the Regional Government to prevent acts of violence against women and children.
20. Protection is all service actions to guarantee and protect the rights of victims of violence organized by the Integrated Service Center.
21. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security for women carried out by family members, police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
22. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
23. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
24. Women's Empowerment is any effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social capacity, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities.
25. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has expertise in accompanying victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of violence victims.
26. Spiritual guidance is accompaniment in the form of services for spiritual strengthening so that sick people can rise to be closer to God so that feelings of calm, security arise, and mental health is achieved.
27. Judicial body is the general judiciary that has the authority to receive, examine, and adjudicate, as well as resolve every case submitted to it, to realize law enforcement and justice.
7 2015
28. Prosecution is the action of the public prosecutor to transfer a case to the competent district court in the manner and according to the procedure regulated by law with a request to be examined and decided by a judge in a court session.
29. Lawsuit is notification accompanied by a request by an interested party to a judge to take action according to law against someone who has harmed them in a civil manner.
30. Institution is an agency/office/body/office within the scope of regional government and/or non-governmental organization (NGO) that provides assistance to victims of violence.
31. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence.
32. Regional Action Plan is the foundation and guideline for related agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in order to carry out activities for the prevention and protection of children and women victims of violence.

36. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
37. Household is husband, wife, and children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, foster care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household.
38. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
39. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD is the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of Bantul Regency
40. Gender responsive budget is a budget that provides and accommodates justice and equality for women and men to access and obtain access, as well as benefits from development programs and participate in decision-making processes and have control over resources.
8 2015
41. Forum for Protection of Violence Victims hereinafter abbreviated as FPKK is a coordination forum for handling Child and Women victims of violence whose implementation is carried out in a networked manner.

1. The provisions of Article 1 are amended, to read as follows: Article 1
1. Government is the Central Government.
2. Region is Bantul Regency.
3. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of regional government administration.
5 2015
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Bantul Regency as an element of Regional Government administration.
5. Regent is the Regent of Bantul.
6. Regional Apparatus Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is the regional apparatus work unit of Bantul Regency.
7. Woman is a person who is female by sex and a person who is recognized by law as a woman.
8. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 years of age, including a child still in the womb.
9. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, and psychological, threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life against the victim.
10. Violence against women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
11. Violence against children is any action that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, psychologically, sexually, neglect, exploitation, economically, and other violence.
12. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death.
13. Psychological Violence is any act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person.
14. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
15. Economic Violence is any act that neglects family members in the form of not providing proper living care or maintenance.
16. Exploitation of Children is any act involving children in activities that may harm their welfare and development or endanger the safety of children with the aim of enabling others to obtain economic, sexual, social, or political benefits, including if it contains restrictions or elimination of opportunities for children to obtain their rights.
6 2015
17. Sexual harassment is any action with sexual nuances conveyed through physical or non-physical contact that targets sexual body parts or a person's sexuality, including by using whistles, winking, comments or sexually nuanced speech, displaying pornographic materials and sexual desires, pinching or touching body parts, movements or gestures that are sexual in nature resulting in feelings of discomfort, offense, feeling degraded in dignity, and possibly causing health and safety problems.
18. Victim is a Child and Woman who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence occurring in the area of Bantul Regency.
19. Prevention is direct efforts made by the Regional Government to prevent acts of violence against women and children.
20. Protection is all service actions to guarantee and protect the rights of victims of violence organized by the Integrated Service Center.
21. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security for women carried out by family members, police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
22. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
23. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
24. Women's Empowerment is any effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social capacity, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities.
25. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has expertise in accompanying victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of violence victims.
26. Spiritual guidance is accompaniment in the form of services for spiritual strengthening so that sick people can rise to be closer to God so that feelings of calm, security arise, and mental health is achieved.
27. Judicial body is the general judiciary that has the authority to receive, examine, and adjudicate, as well as resolve every case submitted to it, to realize law enforcement and justice.
7 2015
28. Prosecution is the action of the public prosecutor to transfer a case to the competent district court in the manner and according to the procedure regulated by law with a request to be examined and decided by a judge in a court session.
29. Lawsuit is notification accompanied by a request by an interested party to a judge to take action according to law against someone who has harmed them in a civil manner.
30. Institution is an agency/office/body/office within the scope of regional government and/or non-governmental organization (NGO) that provides assistance to victims of violence.
31. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence.
32. Regional Action Plan is the foundation and guideline for related agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in order to carry out activities for the prevention and protection of children and women victims of violence.
33. Safe House is a shelter for victims, during the assistance process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers of perpetrators in accordance with predetermined standards.
34. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitutes who can provide protection and fulfillment of victims' needs.
35. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter abbreviated as SOP is standard steps that must be taken in protecting victims starting from complaints/identification, rehabilitation, health, social rehabilitation, legal services up to repatriation and social reintegration of witnesses and/or victims.
36. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
37. Household is husband, wife, and children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, foster care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household.
38. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
39. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD is the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of Bantul Regency
40. Gender responsive budget is a budget that provides and accommodates justice and equality for women and men to access and obtain access, as well as benefits from development programs and participate in decision-making processes and have control over resources.

I. GENERAL
As a manifestation of the Regional Government's responsibility in taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce, and eliminate all forms of violence against children and women, Regional Regulation of Bantul Regency Number 15 of 2013 concerning Protection of Children and Women Victims of Violence has been established.
Up to the present time, the aforementioned Regional Regulation has been implemented in the administration of government in the Region. However, in accordance with the supervision mechanism for regional legal products, the Regional Government of the Special Region of Yogyakarta has provided clarification on Regional Regulation of Bantul Regency Number 15 of 2013 concerning Protection of Children and Women Victims of Violence. From the results of the aforementioned clarification, there are several substantive changes that must be followed up with an Amendment to the Regional Regulation.

As a manifestation of the Regional Government's responsibility in taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce, and eliminate all forms of violence against children and women, Regional Regulation of Bantul Regency Number 15 of 2013 concerning Protection of Children and Women Victims of Violence has been established.

Amendment, Regional Regulation of Bantul Regency, Protection, children and women, victims of violence.

I. GENERAL
As a manifestation of the Regional Government's responsibility in taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce, and eliminate all forms of violence against children and women, Regional Regulation of Bantul Regency Number 15 of 2013 concerning Protection of Children and Women Victims of Violence has been established.
Up to the present time, the aforementioned Regional Regulation has been implemented in the administration of government in the Region. However, in accordance with the supervision mechanism for regional legal products, the Regional Government of the Special Region of Yogyakarta has provided clarification on Regional Regulation of Bantul Regency Number 15 of 2013 concerning Protection of Children and Women Victims of Violence. From the results of the aforementioned clarification, there are several substantive changes that must be followed up with an Amendment to the Regional Regulation.
2 2015 Based on the aforementioned considerations, Regional Regulation of Bantul Regency Number 15 of 2013 concerning Protection of Children and Women Victims of Violence needs to be amended in its Articles and explanations.

As a manifestation of the Regional Government's responsibility in taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce, and eliminate all forms of violence against children and women, Regional Regulation of Bantul Regency Number 15 of 2013 concerning Protection of Children and Women Victims of Violence has been established.

I. GENERAL
As a manifestation of the Regional Government's responsibility in taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce, and eliminate all forms of violence against children and women, Regional Regulation of Bantul Regency Number 15 of 2013 concerning Protection of Children and Women Victims of Violence has been established.
Up to the present time, the aforementioned Regional Regulation has been implemented in the administration of government in the Region. However, in accordance with the supervision mechanism for regional legal products, the Regional Government of the Special Region of Yogyakarta has provided clarification on Regional Regulation of Bantul Regency Number 15 of 2013 concerning Protection of Children and Women Victims of Violence. From the results of the aforementioned clarification, there are several substantive changes that must be followed up with an Amendment to the Regional Regulation.

I. GENERAL
As a manifestation of the Regional Government's responsibility in taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce, and eliminate all forms of violence against children and women, Regional Regulation of Bantul Regency Number 15 of 2013 concerning Protection of Children and Women Victims of Violence has been established.
Up to the present time, the aforementioned Regional Regulation has been implemented in the administration of government in the Region. However, in accordance with the supervision mechanism for regional legal products, the Regional Government of the Special Region of Yogyakarta has provided clarification on Regional Regulation of Bantul Regency Number 15 of 2013 concerning Protection of Children and Women Victims of Violence. From the results of the aforementioned clarification, there are several substantive changes that must be followed up with an Amendment to the Regional Regulation.
2 2015 Based on the aforementioned considerations, Regional Regulation of Bantul Regency Number 15 of 2013 concerning Protection of Children and Women Victims of Violence needs to be amended in its Articles and explanations.

I. GENERAL
As a manifestation of the Regional Government's responsibility in taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce, and eliminate all forms of violence against children and women, Regional Regulation of Bantul Regency Number 15 of 2013 concerning Protection of Children and Women Victims of Violence has been established.
Up to the present time, the aforementioned Regional Regulation has been implemented in the administration of government in the Region. However, in accordance with the supervision mechanism for regional legal products, the Regional Government of the Special Region of Yogyakarta has provided clarification on Regional Regulation of Bantul Regency Number 15 of 2013 concerning Protection of Children and Women Victims of Violence. From the results of the aforementioned clarification, there are several substantive changes that must be followed up with an Amendment to the Regional Regulation.
2 2015 Based on the aforementioned considerations, Regional Regulation of Bantul Regency Number 15 of 2013 concerning Protection of Children and Women Victims of Violence needs to be amended in its Articles and explanations.

e. establishing and facilitating PPT;
f. establishing and facilitating FPKK; and
g. conducting monitoring and evaluation.

As a manifestation of the Regional Government's responsibility in taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce, and eliminate all forms of violence against children and women, Regional Regulation of Bantul Regency Number 15 of 2013 concerning Protection of Children and Women Victims of Violence has been established.
Up to the present time, the aforementioned Regional Regulation has been implemented in the administration of government in the Region. However, in accordance with the supervision mechanism for regional legal products, the Regional Government of the Special Region of Yogyakarta has provided clarification on Regional Regulation of Bantul Regency Number 15 of 2013 concerning Protection of Children and Women Victims of Violence. From the results of the aforementioned clarification, there are several substantive changes that must be followed up with an Amendment to the Regional Regulation.
2 2015 Based on the aforementioned considerations, Regional Regulation of Bantul Regency Number 15 of 2013 concerning Protection of Children and Women Victims of Violence needs to be amended in its Articles and explanations.

Article 7
(1) To implement the provisions as referred to in Article 6 letter a, the Regional Government implements victim protection efforts, in the form of:
a. formulating policies regarding the protection of Children and Women from all forms of violence and discrimination;
b. preparing program and activity planning;
c. providing support for facilities and infrastructure;
d. allocating special gender-responsive budgets that support the protection of children and women victims of violence;
e. establishing and facilitating PPT;
f. establishing and facilitating FPKK; and
g. conducting monitoring and evaluation.
(2) In the implementation of the Regional Government's obligations as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regional Government prepares a Regional Action Plan as a basis for SKPD in implementing protection for victims.
(3) The Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (2), constitutes part of the Regional Medium-Term Development Plan (RPJMD).

7 2015

As a manifestation of the Regional Government's responsibility in taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce, and eliminate all forms of violence against children and women, Regional Regulation of Bantul Regency Number 15 of 2013 concerning Protection of Children and Women Victims of Violence has been established.

As a manifestation of the Regional Government's responsibility in taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce, and eliminate all forms of violence against children and women, Regional Regulation of Bantul Regency Number 15 of 2013 concerning Protection of Children and Women Victims of Violence has been established.
Up to the present time, the aforementioned Regional Regulation has been implemented in the administration of government in the Region. I. GENERAL
As a manifestation of the Regional Government's responsibility in taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce, and eliminate all forms of violence against children and women, Regional Regulation of Bantul Regency Number 15 of 2013 concerning Protection of Children and Women Victims of Violence has been established.
Up to the present time, the aforementioned Regional Regulation has been implemented in the administration of government in the Region. However, in accordance with the supervision mechanism for regional legal products, the Regional Government of the Special Region of Yogyakarta has provided clarification on Regional Regulation of Bantul Regency Number 15 of 2013 concerning Protection of Children and Women Victims of Violence. From the results of the aforementioned clarification, there are several substantive changes that must be followed up with an Amendment to the Regional Regulation.
2 2015 Based on the aforementioned considerations, Regional Regulation of Bantul Regency Number 15 of 2013 concerning Protection of Children and Women Victims of Violence needs to be amended in its Articles and explanations.

Article 7
(1) To implement the provisions as referred to in Article 6 letter a, the Regional Government implements victim protection efforts, in the form of:
a. formulating policies regarding the protection of Children and Women from all forms of violence and discrimination;
b. preparing program and activity planning;
c. providing support for facilities and infrastructure;
d. allocating special gender-responsive budgets that support the protection of children and women victims of violence;
e. establishing and facilitating PPT;
f. establishing and facilitating FPKK; and
g. conducting monitoring and evaluation.
(2) In the implementation of the Regional Government's obligations as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regional Government prepares a Regional Action Plan as a basis for SKPD in implementing protection for victims.
(3) The Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (2), constitutes part of the Regional Medium-Term Development Plan (RPJMD).
(4) Further provisions regarding the Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be further regulated by Regent Regulation.
